name: SikaShield® P44 PE Defend RT 4 mm

cl.x: Provide SikaShield® P44 PE Defend RT 4 mm where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 02.02).

cl.c: Data sheet page 1: Description
cl.x: SikaShield® P44 PE Defend RT 4 mm is an APP modified bituminous waterproofing membrane with a thickness of 4 mm. It contains an anti-root additive, which allows the membrane to be in direct contact with the soil. It is reinforced with a non-woven polyester fabric dimensionally stabilised with glass fibre and is flexible at -10 °C. The underside of the product has a burn-off film for easy torch-application.

cl.c: Data sheet page 1: Uses
cl.l: The Product is used as a waterproofing membrane for:
s: Balconies and terraces under a heavy protection layer such as tiles or gravel.
Flat and sloped roofs under protective layers or ballast
Roof gardens
Roof garden with final waterproofing layer in contact with soil
Car park decks
Wet areas
Basements and other below ground structures
Horizontal reinforced concrete slabs, decks and podiums
Vertical reinforced concrete walls

cl.c: Data sheet page 2: Product Information > Storage conditions
cl.l: The Product must be stored in original unopened and undamaged packaging in dry conditions and temperatures between +5 °C and +35 °C. Protect the Product from direct weather exposure and sunlight. Store in a vertical position. Pallets may be stacked on top of the rolls if all following conditions are met:
s: The rolls have a wooden board on top, separating them from the pallet above.
The weight of the pallet above is equal to or less than the weight of the rolls.

cl.x: Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 02.02) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.

cl.c: Data sheet page 3: Application Instructions > Substrate Quality > SYSTEM DESIGN
cl.l: Consider the following when designing the system:
s: The supporting structure must be of sufficient structural strength to support all new and existing layers of the system build-up.
If used as a roof system, the complete system must be designed to withstand and be secured against wind uplift loadings.

cl.c: Data sheet page 3: Application Instructions > Substrate Condition
cl.x: The substrate surface must be uniform, firm, smooth and free of any sharp protrusion or burrs, clean, dry, free of grease, laitance, oil, dust and loosely adhering particles.

cl.c: Data sheet page 3: Application Instructions > Substrate Preparation > PRIMING
s: 1.Apply Sika® Igolflex P-10+ primer at a rate of 6-8m2 per litre. Note: Consumption rates will vary depending onsubstrate type and porosity.
2. Allow the primer to dry before membrane installation

cl.x: Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 02.02) and the requirements below.

cl.c: Data sheet page 2: Product Information > Effective thickness
Data sheet page 3: Application Instructions > Application > Unrolling at low temperatures
s: At low temperatures, the membrane becomes less flexible.
1. Be careful when unrolling to avoid damaging the membrane.

cl.c: Data sheet page 3: Application Instructions > Application > Damage through footwear
s: Footwear with spikes or sharp protrusions may puncture the membrane.
1. Use footwear with a flat profile when walking over the membrane.

cl.c: Data sheet page 3: Application Instructions > Application > Damage through overheating
s: The polyester melts at +260 °C. If it is damaged through overheating, the membrane becomes unusable.
1. Keep moving the flame while torching to avoid overheating the membrane.

cl.t: Application - Reduced adhesion through insufficient heating
cl.c: Data sheet page 3: Application Instructions > Application > Reduced adhesion through insufficient heating
s: Make sure to heat the membrane sufficiently. If it is not sufficiently heated, the adhesion to the substrate, between layers or on the overlaps will be reduced.
1. If the membrane does not adhere to other elements, lift and retorch the unbonded areas.

cl.c: Data sheet page 3: Application Instructions > Application > Application at less than +5 °C
cl.x: When applying the membranes at temperatures lower than +5 °C, use heating equipment to ensure that the substrate temperature is within the given temperature range.

cl.c: Data sheet page 3: Application Instructions > Application > Application on sloped surfaces
cl.x: For slopes with an inclination greater than 15 %, multi-layered roofs must be carefully designed and, if necessary, integrated with mechanical fastenings.

cl.c: Data sheet page 4: Application Instructions > Application > Seasonal symbol
cl.x: Note: If a seasonal symbol is printed on the roll’s label, it is advisable to use the membrane during the indicated season.

cl.c: Data sheet page 4: Application Instructions > Application > Tackiness at high temperatures
cl.x: Note: When laying the membrane at high temperatures, the integral adhesive will become 'tacky' and may restrict laying operations.

cl.c: Data sheet page 4: Application Instructions > Application > Avoid coinciding joints
s: To avoid coinciding joints, lay the membranes parallel to one another. When applying on another bituminous membrane, make sure to straddle the overlaps of the previous layer.
1. Unroll the membrane.
2. Align the membrane.
3. Re-roll the membrane before application.

cl.c: Data sheet page 4: Application Instructions > Application > MEMBRANE OVERLAPS
s: 1. Overlap the membranes by a minimum of 100 mm on the sides and 150 mm on each end or as specified by the supplier.
2. At the end overlap, cut off a corner measuring 100 mm per side at an angle of 45°.

cl.c: Data sheet page 4: Application Instructions > Application > TORCHING
s: 1. Heat the substrate and the backing film on the underside of the membrane with a gas burner.
2. When the backing film starts to melt, the membrane is ready to stick.
3. Roll the heated membrane forward and press it firmly against the substrate to bond it.
4. Make sure a bead of melted bitumen is visible along the full length of the overlap sides and ends when laying.

cl.c: Data sheet page 4: Application Instructions > Application > Suitable substrates for torching
s: Concrete
Perlite screed
Bituminous membranes with a smooth surface
Coatings (check the compatibility)
Brick masonry
Cementitious screeds

cl.c: Data sheet page 4: Application Instructions > Application > DETAILING
s: 1. Use a sharp knife to cut in all details such as internal and external corners, upstands, vent pipes, drains, support metalwork etc.
Refer to the relevant method statement for further information on detailing.
